title: Retail checkout across AWS, Azure, OCI, and an on-premises database
summary: Trace a customer checkout from an AWS storefront through Azure payments and an OCI order service to an on-premises Oracle database without collapsing metrics, logs, and traces into one ambiguous contract.

ownership.communityAuthor: Owns the topology hypothesis, reproducible synthetic evidence, runbook, and public-source citations.
ownership.projectMaintainer: Owns schema conformance, editorial quality, security review, discovery mappings, and merge decisions.

interlocks.reason: Localize cross-cloud route, DNS, tunnel, and egress failures.
Join symptoms into one incident timeline without mixing signal ownership.
Follow one checkout across service and cloud boundaries.
Relate customer impact to the failing service boundary.

topology.serviceLevelObjective: 99.9% successful checkout completion with p95 end-to-end latency below 2.5 seconds over a rolling 30-day window.

environments.egress: Controlled HTTPS OTLP and structured-log export
Controlled HTTPS OTLP and event export
OCI service identity with private or service-gateway paths

environments.runtime: Oracle Database behind an enterprise network boundary
environments.egress: Management Gateway or controlled outbound HTTPS

route: AWS Cart API → Azure payment adapter
Azure payment adapter → OCI Order API
OCI Order API → on-premises Oracle Database
Telemetry collectors → governed metric, log, and trace destinations

metrics.name: http.server.request.duration
metrics.failureThreshold: p95 > 1.2 s for 10 minutes on any checkout service

metrics.name: http.client.request.duration
metrics.failureThreshold: p95 > 800 ms for a cross-cloud dependency for 10 minutes

metrics.name: kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total
metrics.failureThreshold: increase > 3 restarts in 15 minutes for a checkout component

metrics.name: container_cpu_usage_seconds_total
metrics.failureThreshold: sustained utilization above 85% of the configured CPU limit for 15 minutes

metrics.name: CpuUtilization
metrics.source: OCI service metric namespace appropriate to the emitting resource
metrics.failureThreshold: mean > 85% for 15 minutes after confirming the namespace returns datapoints

metrics.name: db.client.operation.duration
metrics.failureThreshold: p95 > 500 ms for order write operations for 10 minutes

logs.owner: Oracle Log Analytics (Logan) for parsed log and event records
logs.retentionRule: Store only approved operational fields; exclude payment data, credentials, prompts, and customer-identifying payloads.

traces.transport: OpenTelemetry Protocol through an approved collector and private ingest credential
traces.samplingRule: Retain all failed synthetic checkouts and an approved probabilistic sample of successful checkouts.

boundaries.logan: Logan owns parsed log and event records. Prometheus exporter output may be collected as records for investigation, but Logan does not become the authoritative metric backend.
boundaries.prometheus: Prometheus owns time-series samples, labels, recording rules, and exporter health. Exemplars may carry trace_id for navigation.
boundaries.apm: APM owns trace and span topology, duration, status, RUM, and synthetic evidence. It links to logs by trace_id without adopting Logan metadata.

failurePoints.symptom: Checkout latency rises while pod CPU and restart counts increase.
failurePoints.firstAction: Confirm whether saturation, restart churn, or a downstream wait dominates the affected traces.

failurePoints.symptom: Payment calls time out or return an elevated error ratio.
failurePoints.firstAction: Use trace_id to separate payment-provider rejection from network or adapter latency.

failurePoints.symptom: The payment adapter cannot reach the OCI Order API.
failurePoints.firstAction: Validate DNS, route, egress policy, and destination policy before changing application configuration.

failurePoints.symptom: A deployment raises 5xx responses and span error status.
failurePoints.firstAction: Compare pre- and post-deployment error and latency evidence, then follow the approved rollback decision.

failurePoints.symptom: Order writes slow while database sessions wait on contention.
failurePoints.firstAction: Correlate the slow span to database-side session and wait evidence using an approved non-sensitive operation identifier.

failurePoints.symptom: Application health appears normal but trace coverage drops.
failurePoints.firstAction: Treat missing telemetry as collection degradation, not service health, and restore the exporter queue or destination path.

prerequisites: Named service owners and an incident commander for the checkout journey.
Synchronized UTC clocks and consistent service.name values across all environments.
OpenTelemetry instrumentation and collector health metrics in each Kubernetes environment.
Approved IAM, network egress, encryption, and retention policies for every telemetry handoff.
A Logan parser/source association for each approved structured log and event record.
Metric scrape targets and recording rules validated in the authoritative metric backend.
A privacy-safe synthetic checkout that emits a deterministic scenario_run_id.
steps: Detect customer impact from the synthetic checkout and SLO burn signal.
Open the failing trace and identify the first unhealthy service boundary.
Pivot by trace_id and UTC window into Logan for related logs and change events.
Inspect Prometheus or OCI Monitoring metrics in their authoritative backend for saturation, restarts, and collector loss.
Assign the failing boundary to its service owner and follow the mapped Interlock runbook.
Validate recovery with a new synthetic checkout and record the incident evidence without customer payloads.
workflow.emptyResult: A zero-row query or missing trace is inconclusive. Verify permissions, tenancy or account, region, time window, clock skew, parser and source association, collector/exporter health, field mappings, and correlation-key propagation before concluding that an event did not occur.
